freeform_notes:
Quick morning scratchpad for the Microfly series - rough thinking, not a canonical report.

Observations so far:
- Cache helps most for multi-turn (FLY-02, FLY-06) but warmup time matters.
- FLY-03 shows big p99 spikes when many concurrent warm contexts hit the same shard; suspect kernel contention on A100s (see GH PR 428 bench harness).
- FLY-05 quant drop: some hallucination cases in QA v2 after q4_0 conversion; need to pin a small eval set.
- Cost numbers are ballpark (runtime meters + token price estimates).

Questions to resolve:
- Are jitter windows correlated with autoscaler scale events? (ask SRE)
- Can we simulate more realistic traffic (small bursts) on the perf harness? (ticketed in ENG-872)

Quick reminders to self:
- annotate FLY-01 with seed + randomization details after next run
- keep sample outputs in /tmp/microfly-samples/ with naming convention <id>_<ts>.json

Notes about measurement: use 95th percentile for SLA alarms but record p99 separately for incident postmortems. Latency numbers measured from client-side timing in the harness; need to add server-side tracing correlation ids next pass.
